title: 7 Best Pressure Washers in 2026: Gas and Electric by Job
metaDescription: The Simpson MegaShot MS60763 is the best pressure washer for most homes at 3,100 PSI and 2.4 GPM; the Ryobi RY142300 is the top electric. 7 machines ranked.
keywords: best power washer for decks, fence and siding
intro:
The best pressure washer for most homes is the Simpson MegaShot MS60763, a gas machine rated at 3,100 PSI and 2.4 GPM on a Honda GC190 engine, with enough flow to clean a two-car driveway in a morning. If your chores are cars, siding, decks and patios, the Ryobi RY142300 brushless electric is the better buy.

Most people buy too much machine or too little. A homeowner who washes a car and a patio set twice a year does not need a gas engine going stale in the shed, and someone with a long driveway and a two-story house will lose a Saturday to a small electric. This guide ranks seven gas and electric pressure washers, then covers PSI versus GPM, gas versus electric, surface-by-surface settings, durable pumps, accessories, safe use and winter storage.
quickAnswer: Buy the Simpson MegaShot MS60763 for driveways, siding and decks, the Generac SpeedWash 3200 for the most flow per dollar, and the Simpson PowerShot only for weekly or paid work. For cars, decks and siding, buy the Ryobi RY142300 or, for painted finishes, the Karcher K5 Premium Smart Control. The Sun Joe SPX3000 suits light jobs on a tight budget.

Multiply PSI by GPM before you trust any box. That product, called cleaning units, predicts how fast a machine finishes far better than pressure alone.

If two of your three most common jobs are concrete or a whole-house wash, buy gas, and the Simpson MegaShot is the default. If they are cars, decks, siding or furniture, buy a good electric like the Ryobi RY142300 and add a surface cleaner for the occasional patio.

sections.heading: The 7 Best Pressure Washers in 2026, Ranked
sections.body:
These rankings draw on manufacturer ratings for pressure, flow, engine or motor type and pump design, plus warranty terms, parts availability and recurring themes in owner feedback. Each machine is placed by how well it fits a realistic household job list. None were put through hands-on trials for this guide, and no brand paid for placement.

### Best Overall: Simpson MegaShot MS60763
The MegaShot MS60763 is the gas pressure washer most homeowners should price first. Simpson rates it at 3,100 PSI and 2.4 GPM, about 7,400 cleaning units, which is enough to clear a two-car concrete driveway in a morning with a surface cleaner on the wand. It runs on a Honda GC190, a residential overhead-cam engine known for easy starts and backed by a parts network that reaches almost everywhere. A welded steel frame and 10-inch pneumatic tires make it easier to roll across gravel and lawn than plastic-wheeled machines. It comes with quick-connect tips for the standard spray angles plus a soap nozzle. The pump is an axial cam design, normal at this level, which means it is built for weekend jobs rather than daily contract work. For a house, driveway, deck and fence on a typical suburban lot, it hits the balance point between flow, engine reliability and price.

**Pros:** Honda GC190 engine with wide parts support; about 7,400 cleaning units; steel frame and pneumatic wheels; full set of quick-connect tips.
**Cons:** Axial cam pump is not built for daily pro use; loud, with fuel, oil and winter prep; too strong for casual car washing without care.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Simpson+MegaShot+MS60763&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Electric: Ryobi RY142300 2300 PSI Brushless
The RY142300 is the plug-in that gives up the least to gas in everyday chores. Ryobi rates it at 2,300 PSI and 1.2 GPM from a brushless motor, which the company positions as quieter and longer-lived than the brushed universal motors in most budget electrics. It stands upright on a compact wheeled frame, stores its hose and cord on board, and uses standard quick-connect fittings, so third-party surface cleaners and wands attach without adapters. At about 2,760 cleaning units, it handles cars, vinyl siding, patio furniture, patios and wood decks comfortably. Concrete is doable but slow, and a small surface cleaner helps a lot there. The appeal for most buyers is simple: no fuel, no oil, no pull cord, and you can run it on a weeknight without bothering the neighbors much. It still needs a GFCI outlet within reach of the cord and pump protection before a freeze.

**Pros:** Brushless motor runs quieter and is built for longer life; upright frame with on-board storage; standard quick-connect fittings; no engine upkeep.
**Cons:** 1.2 GPM makes big concrete jobs slow; needs a GFCI outlet in cord reach; pump still needs winter protection.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Ryobi+RY142300+2300+PSI+brushless+pressure+washer&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Gas Value: Generac SpeedWash 3200 PSI
Generac built the SpeedWash 3200 around one idea: stop walking back to swap nozzles. Its PowerDial gun rotates between spray patterns and a soap setting at the handle, so going from a wide rinse to a tighter cleaning stream takes a twist. Generac rates it at 3,200 PSI and 2.7 GPM, about 8,600 cleaning units, which is more flow than many gas machines in its price range and translates directly into faster rinsing on concrete and siding. The kit typically includes quick-connect extras such as a surface cleaner, rotating brush and foam cannon, so it can be a complete setup out of the box. It uses Generac's own overhead-valve engine rather than a Honda, which matters mostly for long-term parts sourcing at local shops. Its axial cam pump keeps it in homeowner territory. If you want strong flow and a convenient gun without paying for a triplex pump, it is a smart buy.

**Pros:** 2.7 GPM rinses faster than most consumer gas units; PowerDial gun changes patterns at the handle; bundle often includes useful attachments.
**Cons:** Generac engine has a smaller service network than Honda; axial cam pump limits it to homeowner duty; heavier than electrics.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Generac+SpeedWash+3200+PSI+pressure+washer&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Budget: Sun Joe SPX3000 2030 PSI
The SPX3000 has been one of the best-selling pressure washers for years because it handles light jobs for very little money. Sun Joe lists maximum figures of 2,030 PSI and 1.76 GPM; as with most budget electrics, those peaks do not happen at the same moment, so treat it as a light-duty machine. It uses a universal motor, which is louder and wears faster than induction or brushless designs. Two on-board detergent tanks with a selector switch let you jump between a car soap and a patio cleaner without refilling. Five quick-connect tips come in the box, and automatic shut-off stops the pump when you release the trigger. It is light enough to carry up porch steps. It suits cars, bikes, grills, patio furniture and small patios well. It is the wrong choice if you plan to strip a deck or clean a long driveway several times a year, and the included hose is short.

**Pros:** Very low price for a capable light-duty washer; two detergent tanks with selector; five tips included; light to carry.
**Cons:** Universal motor is loud and shorter-lived; peak ratings overstate real cleaning speed; plastic build and short hose.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Sun+Joe+SPX3000+pressure+washer&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Heavy-Duty: Simpson PowerShot PS60869
The PowerShot line is where a homeowner pressure washer becomes a light commercial tool. The PS60869 pairs a Honda GX engine, the commercial family with a cast-iron cylinder sleeve, with a triplex plunger pump. A triplex pump uses three ceramic plungers on a crankshaft and can be resealed and rebuilt, so it is designed to run for many hundreds of hours instead of being thrown away when it wears. Simpson rates the machine in the 4,000-PSI-plus class with high flow, which puts it well above the MegaShot in cleaning units. That much energy is overkill for a car and can gouge soft wood quickly in careless hands, but it is exactly right for someone who cleans large concrete pads, farm equipment, long fence lines or several properties. It costs roughly double a residential gas unit, is heavy and loud, and needs real storage space. If you would run it weekly, the rebuildable pump justifies the price.

**Pros:** Rebuildable triplex plunger pump; commercial Honda GX engine; very high cleaning units for big concrete; heavy steel frame and large wheels.
**Cons:** Roughly double the cost of a residential gas unit; heavy and loud; easy to damage wood and siding without care.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Simpson+PowerShot+PS60869&tag=sktiger-20)

### Gentlest on Paint: Karcher K5 Premium Smart Control
Karcher's K5 Premium Smart Control is the electric for people who care about the finish on what they clean. Karcher rates it around 2,000 PSI and 1.4 GPM from a water-cooled induction motor, a design that runs cooler and quieter than budget universal motors. Its signature feature is a trigger gun with a small display and selectable pressure levels, so you can step down for car paint and glass and back up for patio stone without changing tips. The Smart Control app pairs with the gun and suggests settings for different surfaces. A built-in hose reel and tall upright frame keep storage tidy. The main drawback is that Karcher uses its own connection system on parts of the setup, so some third-party accessories need adapters. It is also pricey for a 2,000 PSI machine and slow on large concrete. For detailing cars, washing painted siding and cleaning outdoor furniture, it is the most controllable machine here.

**Pros:** Pressure adjustable at the gun with a readout; water-cooled induction motor; built-in hose reel; excellent control on paint and glass.
**Cons:** Some proprietary fittings need adapters; pricey for its pressure class; slow on large concrete.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Karcher+K5+Premium+Smart+Control&tag=sktiger-20)

### Most Pressure on a Plug: Greenworks Pro GPW3000 3000 PSI Electric
Greenworks advertises this machine at 3,000 PSI, about as high as plug-in pressure washers go on a standard household circuit. The catch is flow. At roughly 1.1 GPM, its cleaning units land near 3,300, only a little above a good 2,000 PSI electric. The extra pressure earns its keep on small, stubborn spots: tire marks, mildew in brick joints and the grimy corners of a garage slab. It uses an induction motor, longer-lived than universal designs, on a sturdier frame than entry electrics, with on-board storage for tips, hose and cord. On siding, decks and patios it performs much like other mid-range electrics, and on concrete it still benefits from a surface cleaner. Buy it if you want the strongest point pressure available without an engine, and go in understanding that pressure alone does not make a machine finish faster. High pressure also calls for care on wood and siding.

**Pros:** Among the highest PSI ratings on a household circuit; induction motor; sturdier frame and storage than budget electrics; good on stubborn spots.
**Cons:** Low flow keeps overall cleaning speed modest; high pressure needs care on wood and siding; heavier than compact electrics.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Greenworks+Pro+3000+PSI+electric+pressure+washer&tag=sktiger-20)

sections.heading: PSI or GPM: Which Matters More in a Pressure Washer?
sections.body:
PSI tells you how hard the water hits. GPM tells you how much water is doing the work and how fast it carries loosened dirt away. A narrow jet at high pressure cuts a line through grime, then leaves the slurry sitting there. More flow sweeps it off.

### Cleaning units
Multiply PSI by GPM to get cleaning units. It is not a lab standard and it ignores nozzle design, but as a first filter in a store aisle it works.

| Class | Typical cleaning units |
| --- | --- |
| Budget electric | 2,500 to 3,500 |
| Premium electric | 2,800 to 3,500 |
| Residential gas | 7,000 to 9,000 |
| Triplex gas | 12,000 and up |

That is why a 2,700 PSI gas unit at 2.5 GPM finishes a driveway far faster than a 3,000 PSI electric at 1.1 GPM.

### Watch for "max"
Many machines publish peak pressure and unrestricted flow, two numbers that never happen together. Brands that publish rated or working figures certified under the CETA or PWMA standard give you more trustworthy numbers. When a sheet says max PSI and max GPM, assume real performance is noticeably lower.

### Best electric pressure washer by gallons per minute
A standard 15-amp outlet limits a plug-in to roughly 1,800 watts, which caps flow around 1.1 to 1.8 GPM whatever the pressure rating says. Within that ceiling, the Karcher K5 at about 1.4 GPM and the Ryobi RY142300 at 1.2 GPM offer good working flow, and the Sun Joe's 1.76 GPM is a peak figure.

sections.heading: Gas or Electric: Which Pressure Washer Should You Buy?
sections.body:
### What gas gives you
Flow, cordless freedom and the ability to finish a long driveway in one session. In exchange you get noise, 55 to 80 pounds or more of machine, fuel storage, oil changes, winter prep and carbon monoxide.

### What electric gives you
Plug in, connect the hose, and you are washing within a minute. Noise is closer to a loud vacuum, there are no fumes, and storage means draining the pump and rolling it into a corner.

| Factor | Electric | Gas |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typical flow | 1.1 to 1.8 GPM | 2.3 to 4.0 GPM |
| Noise | Moderate | Loud, hearing protection advised |
| Weight | 25 to 50 lb | 55 to 100+ lb |
| Upkeep | Pump care only | Oil, fuel, spark plug, pump care |
| Best for | Cars, siding, decks, patios | Driveways, large decks, whole houses |

### Cordless models
Battery pressure washers solve a different problem: washing a boat at a slip or a car in a parking space, often drawing from a bucket. They do not replace either category above for house and driveway work.

### A quick decision test
List the three jobs you do most. Two of them concrete or whole-house washing: buy gas. Two of them cars, decks, siding or furniture: buy electric. Many households that bought gas for one driveway a year would be happier with an electric for routine work and a rental or pro for the big job.

sections.heading: What Is the Best Pressure Washer for Concrete, Cars, Decks and Siding?
sections.body:
Each surface wants a different amount of force, and tip and distance matter as much as the machine.

### Typical settings by surface
| Surface | Typical PSI | Tip | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Car paint | 1,200 to 1,900 | 40 degree or foam | Stay 18 to 24 in. away |
| Softwood deck | 500 to 1,200 | 25 or 40 degree | Follow the grain |
| Vinyl siding | 1,300 to 1,600 | 25 or 40 degree | Spray downward only |
| Pavers | 1,500 to 2,500 | Surface cleaner | Re-sand joints after |
| Concrete driveway | 2,500 to 3,500 | Surface cleaner | Flow matters most |

### Concrete and driveways
Broom-finished concrete rewards a gas machine with at least 2.3 GPM and a rotating surface cleaner; our [surface cleaner guide](/best-surface-cleaner-for-pressure-washer/) pairs models with machine classes. Oil, rust and tire marks respond to chemistry and dwell time, not more pressure, so pretreat with a product from the [best driveway cleaner](/best-driveway-cleaner/) list or follow the steps for [removing oil stains from a driveway](/how-to-remove-oil-stains-from-driveway/).

### Decks, fences and siding
For decks, fences and siding with algae or mildew, apply a cleaner that kills the growth through the soap nozzle, let it dwell, and rinse at low pressure. Spray siding downward, never up under the laps. A mid-range electric handles all of this well.

### Cars
Use a 40-degree tip or a foam cannon at a distance. The Karcher K5's adjustable gun pressure makes it the safest choice for paint.

### One machine for everything
If one washer must handle both a car and a driveway, buy for the driveway and control force on the car with a wide tip, distance and foam. The reverse does not work: no technique makes a 1.2 GPM electric a fast concrete cleaner, though a small walk and single-car pad are fine with an electric and a surface cleaner.

sections.heading: Which Pressure Washer Has the Most Durable Pump and Motor?
sections.body:
The pump is the part that fails, and pump design largely decides how long a pressure washer lives.

### Axial cam pumps
Most consumer machines use an axial cam pump, also called a wobble or swash plate pump. It is compact and cheap, commonly rated in the low hundreds of hours, and usually replaced rather than repaired when it wears out. For a few weekends a year, that is a fair trade.

### Triplex plunger pumps
Triplex pumps run three ceramic plungers off a crankshaft at lower speed and can be rebuilt with seal and valve kits. Makers commonly rate them for well over a thousand hours. They add significant cost and pay off for weekly use, rental fleets, neighbor jobs or a side business. The Simpson PowerShot is the triplex pick here.

### Engines
Honda's GC series is a residential overhead-cam engine used on many consumer machines; the GX series is the commercial line with a cast-iron cylinder sleeve. Store-brand overhead-valve engines from Generac, Briggs and Stratton, Kohler and others are generally reliable on homeowner machines. What matters most is whether a local shop can get parts.

### Electric motors
Universal motors on budget units are light and cheap but noisy, with carbon brushes that wear out. Induction and brushless motors, used on the Karcher, Greenworks and Ryobi picks, run cooler and quieter and generally last longer.

sections.heading: Which Nozzles and Accessories Are Worth Buying?
sections.body:
### The tip color code
Red is a zero-degree pencil stream, yellow is 15 degrees for stripping, green is 25 degrees for general cleaning, white is 40 degrees for vehicles and soft surfaces, and black is the low-pressure soap tip. Most homeowners can leave red in the box for good.

### Turbo nozzles
A turbo or rotary nozzle spins a zero-degree stream in a fast cone. It is excellent on bare concrete and stubborn stains and too aggressive for wood, siding and paint. Keep it moving and hold it farther back than you think.

### Surface cleaner
The best upgrade for anyone with concrete. It keeps the distance constant, stops zebra stripes, contains overspray and often roughly halves driveway time. Match its rated PSI and GPM range to your machine.

### Other add-ons
A foam cannon earns its keep for car washing. An extension wand reaches second-story siding from the ground, which is far safer than spraying from a ladder. A longer non-kinking hose saves constant repositioning. Before buying, confirm the fittings: usually 1/4-inch quick-connect for tips and M22 or 3/8-inch for hoses.

### After the wash
A clean, dry deck is ready for stain, and washed, dried concrete is ready for sealer. See our [deck stain reviews](/best-deck-stain-reviews/), [concrete driveway sealer reviews](/best-concrete-driveway-sealer-reviews/) and [paver sealer picks](/best-paver-sealer/) if washing is step one of a bigger project.

sections.heading: How Do You Use and Store a Pressure Washer So It Lasts?
sections.body:
### Safety first
Gas engines make carbon monoxide. Run a gas pressure washer outdoors only, never in a garage or shed even with the door open, and aim the exhaust away from windows, doors and vents. High-pressure water can cut skin and inject water under it, an injury that needs emergency care. Never point the wand at people or pets, engage the trigger lock when you set the gun down, and wear closed shoes and eye protection. Plug electrics into a GFCI-protected outlet and test it each session.

### Check your water supply
Time how long a 5-gallon bucket takes to fill from your hose. Under two minutes means roughly 2.5 GPM or more. Starving the pump causes cavitation, pulsing and fast wear. Run water through the pump before starting to purge air.

### Even results
Start with the widest tip, hold a steady distance, and overlap passes by about a third. Apply detergent to siding from the bottom up and rinse from the top down. Do not leave the machine idling in bypass for more than a couple of minutes; recirculating water heats up and damages seals.

### Winter and storage
Pumps die from running dry, freezing and mineral buildup. After each use, release trapped pressure, disconnect the hoses and let the pump drain. Before storage, run pump saver through the inlet. Winterize any machine kept where it freezes, electrics included. For gas units, stabilize the fuel or run the carburetor dry, change the oil on schedule, and check the plug and air filter yearly. Inspect hoses and O-rings each spring, and keep a tip-cleaning wire handy for pulsing caused by clogged tips.

### Rent, buy or hire
One heavy job a year is often cheaper to rent. Owning makes sense at around three or more substantial jobs a season. Two-story homes, roofs and delicate surfaces are often best left to a pro.

mistakes.title: Using the red tip on anything you care about
mistakes.body: The zero-degree tip packs the full force of the pump into a coin-sized point. It carves grooves in wood, etches lines into concrete and causes serious injection injuries on skin. Start with the 40-degree tip, move closer before you go narrower, and reserve red for rare spots on bare metal or masonry.

mistakes.title: Spraying up under siding laps
mistakes.body: Siding sheds water falling down, not water driven upward. Spraying from below forces water behind the panels into sheathing and insulation, where it feeds hidden mold and rot. Keep the wand level or angled down, use detergent and a wide tip, and reach upper stories with an extension wand.

mistakes.title: Buying on PSI alone
mistakes.body: A big PSI number looks impressive, but flow decides how fast you finish. A 3,000 PSI electric at 1.1 GPM delivers far fewer cleaning units than a 2,700 PSI gas unit at 2.3 GPM. Multiply pressure by flow, check whether figures are rated or peak, and buy for the job you do most.

mistakes.title: Running the engine in the garage
mistakes.body: Starting a gas pressure washer just inside the garage door to stay dry is a common route to carbon monoxide poisoning. The gas builds fast, has no smell and drifts into the house. Run the engine outdoors only, well away from doors and windows, with the exhaust pointed away from the building.

mistakes.title: Storing it wet over winter
mistakes.body: One overnight freeze can crack a pump manifold, and you only find out next spring as a leak or no pressure. Drain the pump, run pump saver antifreeze through it, and store the machine above freezing when you can. Electric units need exactly the same care as gas units.

faqs.q: What is the best pressure washer for home use?
faqs.a: The Simpson MegaShot MS60763 is the best pressure washer for most homes with a driveway, siding and a deck. Simpson rates it at 3,100 PSI and 2.4 GPM on a Honda GC190 engine. If your jobs are mostly cars, patios and siding, the Ryobi RY142300 brushless electric is quieter and easier to own. Decide by your three most frequent jobs.

faqs.q: What is the best power washer for decks, fences and siding?
faqs.a: A good electric is the best power washer for decks, fences and siding, because those surfaces need moderate pressure, not raw force. The Ryobi RY142300 and Karcher K5 Premium Smart Control both suit them. Use a 25- or 40-degree tip, apply a cleaner for algae or mildew through the soap nozzle, and spray siding downward only.

faqs.q: Does flow or pressure matter more?
faqs.a: Flow, measured in GPM, predicts how fast you finish. PSI breaks dirt loose; flow carries it away. Multiply the two to get cleaning units, the most useful single figure for comparing machines. For delicate surfaces, moderate PSI with decent flow is safest. For big concrete jobs, put GPM first within your budget.

faqs.q: How much PSI do I need for a concrete driveway?
faqs.a: Most broom-finished concrete driveways clean well at 2,500 to 3,500 PSI, ideally with at least 2.3 GPM and a rotating surface cleaner. A smaller electric can clean concrete but takes much longer and tends to stripe. Pretreat oil and rust stains with the right cleaner, because extra pressure does little to lift them on its own.

faqs.q: Are electric pressure washers good enough?
faqs.a: For cars, outdoor furniture, decks, siding and modest patios, a good electric is more than enough and much easier to own. They fall short on large concrete areas, because a household circuit limits flow to under about 2 GPM. Pair an electric with a small surface cleaner and it handles a walkway and a single-car pad comfortably.

faqs.q: How long does a home pressure washer last?
faqs.a: It depends mostly on the pump and storage. Consumer axial cam pumps are typically rated in the low hundreds of hours, which can mean many years of occasional use if the machine is never frozen or run dry. Triplex pumps are rated much higher and can be rebuilt. Winterizing and pump saver extend life significantly.

faqs.q: Should I rent or buy a pressure washer?
faqs.a: Rent if you have one heavy job a year; a day with a commercial gas unit usually costs less than owning one and skips storage and upkeep. Buy once you have several substantial jobs each season or want to wash cars and furniture whenever you like. Many owners keep an electric for routine work and rent gas for the driveway.

bottomLine: For most homes with a driveway, siding and a deck, the Simpson MegaShot MS60763 is the machine to buy: a dependable Honda engine and enough flow to make concrete go quickly. If your list is mostly cars, patios and siding, the Ryobi RY142300 brushless electric is quieter and needs almost no upkeep, and the Karcher K5 is the gentlest on paint. The Generac SpeedWash gives the most flow per dollar, and only weekly or paid work justifies the triplex-pump PowerShot. Multiply PSI by GPM before trusting a box, use the widest tip that does the job, add a surface cleaner for concrete, and winterize the pump every fall.
